newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- House speaker Jose de Venecia dismisses a news report about a move to oust him from him post as "the usual intrigue and black propaganda". (MANILA TIMES)

- Congressmen reject renewed calls for the scrapping of the countrywide development fund amid findings of the Commission on Audit that six legislators had misused more than 20 million pesos of their allocations. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- President Fidel Ramos maintains the country's economic gains have benefitted a large majority of Filipinos, and says he remains bullish about the Philippines' economic performance during the remaining 13 months of his administration. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Education Secretary Ricardo Gloria says initial reports reaching the Department of Education, Culture and Sports say the opening of classes is generally smooth and orderly. (MANILA BULLETIN)
